subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` for CLI, gateway exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP child processes, or prefer the narrower exec-only SecretRef contract being explored in PR #96309?
rationale: The code appears coherent, but automation cannot choose whether this broad config/env surface is the desired public API and security boundary.

options.title: Choose the canonical env contract before merge
options.body: Require maintainers to decide between this broad literal agent env surface and the exec-only SecretRef direction, then align the PR to that decision before landing.

options.title: Accept the broad per-agent env surface
options.body: Land this PR after checks are green, knowingly making `agents.list[].env` the public API across all child-process families covered by the branch.

options.title: Pause behind the exec-only SecretRef design
options.body: Keep this PR open or close it only after #96309 or a successor proves a narrower contract can satisfy the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Choose the canonical env contract before merge
recommendation.body: Require maintainers to decide between this broad literal agent env surface and the exec-only SecretRef direction, then align the PR to that decision before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review and recent config/gateway work make this the best available owner signal for the product/security contract decision.
